public_rationale: Launch testing supports the practical complaint: Operator failed tasks, produced unsuitable results and required substantial help. It also completed real browser tasks in independent testing. The evidence supports severe usability and reliability limitations, while limiting the broader suggestion that the product scarcely worked. Later improvements play no part in this assessment.
limitations: Successful simple tasks do not establish dependable completion of harder tasks.
Slow or frustrating completion is distinct from failure.
The qualitative wording makes the overall boundary interpretive.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's Operator agent is barely functional and does not seem to work.

statement.excerpt: The launch of its "Operator" "agent" was a joke — a barely-functional product that is allegedly meant to control your computer and take distinct actions, but doesn't seem to work.

from_speaker: control your computer and take distinct actions
our_interpretation: Assess the January 2025 launch version, from launch through the post date.
Read the criticism as alleging severe practical unreliability in advertised browser tasks, not mathematically zero successful actions.
Exclude 'was a joke' as an evaluative description.
Operator's advertised scope was its own browser. Full desktop control and later ChatGPT agent versions are outside the product assessment.
No success-rate threshold is supplied; weigh observed completion, failures and required intervention without inventing one.
criteria.support_condition: Independent launch-version tests show serious failures or extensive intervention on ordinary advertised browser tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent launch-version tests demonstrate useful completed tasks, materially limiting the broad suggestion that the product scarcely functioned.

evidence.explanation: The tester reports five failures involving web research and online tools. These show real launch limitations, but the small, relatively demanding task set is not a representative consumer success-rate estimate.

evidence.locator: Hands-on review, paragraph introducing the London walking-tour task
evidence.explanation: Newton describes successful browser research producing walking-tour links and a completed lesson-plan task. His same review documents substantial shopping friction, so these successes limit the broad dismissal without establishing reliable autonomy.

evidence.locator: Section 'When Operator Almost Shines', final paragraph
evidence.explanation: This firsthand browser-research test returned unsuitable results despite a lengthy run. The review also describes poor product research, supporting the criticism of practical unreliability.
The underlying model completed substantial shares of benchmark tasks. These company-run evaluations are not measurements of the launch product's reliability for ordinary users.
